name: ActivityWatch
tagline: See where your computer time goes with automatic tracking that keeps your data local.
description:
ActivityWatch is an automatic, open-source time tracker designed around local data ownership. Its background watchers record the active application, window title, and whether the computer is in use, then present the timeline in a browser-based dashboard running on the Mac.

## Features

- Track active applications and window titles automatically.
- Detect away time so unattended minutes are separated from active computer use.
- Add browser extensions for more detailed website and tab tracking.
- Review timelines, daily activity, categories, and time totals in local dashboards.
- Create rules that classify activities into projects or meaningful groups.
- Extend collection and analysis with community watchers and a local REST API.

## Where it fits

ActivityWatch is useful for personal time audits, attention analysis, and reconstructing a workday without sending the history to a hosted tracker. It requires more setup and interpretation than a manual timer. Automatic titles and URLs can also capture sensitive context, so exclusions and retention deserve deliberate attention.

## Privacy and requirements

Data is stored locally in SQLite and is not uploaded by default. The local ActivityWatch API has no authentication and is not designed to be exposed to a network or shared multi-user machine. Stable Mac releases support Intel; Apple-silicon builds may be marked pre-release, so check the download label for the current architecture.

## Pricing

ActivityWatch is free and open source under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.
